question: A traveling consultant reaches internal applications through the company's clientless SSL/TLS VPN portal. Which port must the hotel's firewall allow outbound for this session to work?
explanation: SSL/TLS VPNs run over TCP port 443, the same port as HTTPS, so they pass through nearly any network that allows secure web browsing. UDP 500 carries the IKE negotiation for IPsec VPNs, TCP 22 is SSH, and TCP 80 is unencrypted HTTP, which a TLS session does not use.

question: A router has a mean time between failures of 8,760 hours and a mean time to repair of 4 hours. What is its availability, rounded to two decimal places?
explanation: Availability is the mean time between failures divided by the sum of the mean time between failures and the mean time to repair: 8,760 divided by 8,764 is 0.99954, or 99.95 percent. An availability of 99.9 percent would allow almost 9 hours of downtime in a year and 99.5 percent almost 44 hours, while 99.99 percent would allow less than one hour.

question: A remote employee's laptop runs VPN software that connects it to the office over the internet and gives it an address on the corporate subnet. Which type of VPN is this?
explanation: A client-to-site VPN runs software on one device that builds a tunnel to the corporate VPN concentrator and gives the device an internal address, so it works as if it were in the office. A site-to-site VPN joins whole networks through their gateways, a clientless VPN gives browser access to web applications without an internal address, and an MPLS VPN is a carrier service that links sites.

question: How does a dictionary attack differ from a brute force attack when guessing a password?
options: It tries username and password pairs from old breaches
It tries each word in a list of likely passwords
It tries character strings in sequence up to a set length
It tries one common password on many accounts
explanation: A dictionary attack limits its guesses to a list of words and known passwords, which makes it fast against common choices but useless against a random string that is not on the list. A brute force attack works through character combinations in sequence, password spraying tries a few common passwords across many accounts, and credential stuffing replays username and password pairs leaked from other breaches.

question: An administrator enables BPDU guard on the PortFast access ports of an office switch. A week later, BPDU guard has disabled one of these ports. What happened at that port?
options: A device with an unlisted MAC address was connected
A device that sends spanning tree frames was connected
A device that draws too much power was connected
A device that floods broadcast frames was connected
explanation: BPDU guard disables a PortFast port as soon as it receives a spanning tree BPDU, which shows that a switch has been attached where only an end device belongs. An unlisted MAC address is a matter for port security, and a flood of broadcasts is a matter for storm control. A device that draws too much power trips the PoE overload protection of the port, which has no connection with spanning tree.

question: A technician has finished gathering information about a fault and is now deciding whether to work up from the physical layer, work down from the application layer, or start in the middle of the OSI model. In CompTIA's methodology, which step is the technician in?
options: Test the theory to determine the cause
Establish a theory of probable cause
explanation: CompTIA lists the OSI-based approaches (top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top and divide and conquer) under establish a theory of probable cause, alongside questioning the obvious, because they guide which causes the technician considers first. Gathering information belongs to identifying the problem, which is finished here, testing needs a theory to test, and a plan of action is made only after the cause has been confirmed.

question: A design studio wants one appliance on its Ethernet LAN that presents shared folders to Windows and Mac computers over SMB. Which type of storage is this?
explanation: Network-attached storage is a file server appliance that joins the LAN and shares folders at file level through protocols such as SMB and NFS. A storage area network instead presents block-level volumes to servers, usually over Fibre Channel or iSCSI. Direct-attached storage connects to a single computer and not to the network, and cloud-based object storage is a provider's service reached over the internet.

question: A company addresses a WAN link with 10.1.1.0/30 and a LAN with 10.1.2.0/24. RIPv1 cannot advertise both correctly, but RIPv2 can. Which feature of RIPv2 makes the difference?
options: A metric based on link bandwidth
explanation: RIPv2 carries the subnet mask of every route in its updates, so prefixes of different lengths, such as a /30 and a /24, can be advertised correctly. RIPv1 sends no mask, so the receiving router has to assume one. Both versions use hop count as the metric and treat 16 hops as unreachable, and IPv6 prefixes need a separate protocol, RIPng. RIPv2 also added authentication and multicast updates.

question: A certifier reports a near-end crosstalk failure on a new Cat 6 link, measured at the patch panel end, while every other test passes. What is the most likely cause?
options: A run that exceeds the maximum length
A kink that changes the cable's impedance
A conductor broken inside the cable jacket
explanation: Near-end crosstalk is signal coupling from one pair into another close to the transmitter, and the usual cause of a failure at one end is pairs untwisted too far back where they were terminated. An over-length run fails insertion loss and length, a kink shows up as a return loss failure, and a broken conductor fails the wire map, so none of them fits a link whose only failure is crosstalk.

question: A company grants network permissions to job groups, not to individual people: the accounting group reaches only the accounting servers, and only the IT group reaches the management interfaces of switches and servers. Anyone who changes jobs moves into the new job's group. Which access control model is this?
explanation: Role-based access control ties permissions to job roles such as accounting or IT, so a person's access follows the role and changes when the role changes. Rule-based access control applies conditions such as the time of day or the source address to every request, whoever makes it, mandatory access control compares classification labels with clearances, and discretionary access control lets each resource's owner decide who may use it.

question: A mail server answers ICMP echo requests, but users cannot send mail through it. From a workstation, which command can open a connection to the server's TCP port 25 to show whether the mail service is accepting connections?
explanation: A Telnet client opens a TCP connection to whatever port it is given, so a command such as telnet 10.0.0.25 25 shows at once whether the service answers. Ping uses ICMP, which has no ports, so a reply proves only that the host is up. Tracert maps the routers on the path, and nslookup queries DNS, which can confirm the server's address but not the state of its mail port.

question: On a legacy bus network, every station loses connectivity at the same moment. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A loop between two of the switches
A station that is switched off
A break in the backbone cable
A failure of the central switch
explanation: On a bus, every station shares one backbone cable, so a break anywhere in it (or a missing terminator) reflects the signal and stops all stations at once. A central switch failure has that effect on a star, a station that is switched off does not interrupt a bus, and a switching loop needs redundant links between switches, which a bus does not have.

question: During an acquisition, employees of the acquired firm are shown the buyer's customer lists and unreleased product designs. Before the first meeting, each must sign a legal document promising not to reveal that information. Which document is this?
explanation: A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) is a contract in which the signer promises to keep specified information confidential. A service-level agreement (SLA) sets performance targets for a service. A memorandum of understanding (MOU) records the shared intentions of two parties, and an acceptable use policy (AUP) sets the rules for using an organization's systems.

question: Some receiving mail servers reject messages from a company's new mail server because a DNS lookup of the server's IP address, 203.0.113.25, returns no host name. Which record type needs to be added?
explanation: A PTR record in the reverse lookup zone maps an IP address back to a host name, and many mail servers refuse messages from a sending address that has none. An MX record tells other servers where to deliver mail for the domain, a CNAME record makes one name an alias of another, and an NS record names the servers that are authoritative for a zone.

question: An attacker sends one request to a company's DNS server and receives every record the server holds for the domain, including all hostnames, addresses and mail servers. What has the attacker performed?
explanation: A zone transfer copies every record in a DNS zone in one exchange, so a server that allows transfers to any host hands an attacker a map of the network. Subdomain brute forcing finds names by guessing them one query at a time, cache poisoning plants false records in a resolver, and pharming redirects users to a fake site. Allowing transfers only to the secondary servers prevents the leak.

question: A coffee shop's guest Wi-Fi hands out leases from one /24 scope on its router, each lasting eight days. By midweek, new customers join the SSID but receive no IP configuration, while devices that joined earlier still work. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: A /24 scope holds at most 254 addresses, and with eight-day leases every phone that has passed through keeps its address long after it leaves, so the pool runs out and new clients get no lease; a shorter lease fixes it. A rogue server would hand out wrong addresses rather than none, a wrong VLAN would cut off every device, and no relay agent is involved when the router itself runs DHCP.

question: A weekly report lists the five hosts that sent the most data across a company's WAN link, and it shows that one host accounts for 40 percent of the total. Which activity does this report represent?
explanation: Traffic analysis studies flow data to show which hosts, applications and conversations use a link and how much, which is how the heaviest users are found. Log aggregation gathers event messages from many devices in one place, and network discovery finds and lists the devices that are on the network. Availability monitoring checks that devices and services are up and answering.

question: A desk phone connects to a switch access port, and a PC connects through the phone. On that one port, the call traffic must travel tagged in its own VLAN while the PC traffic stays untagged. Which feature is configured on the port?
explanation: A voice VLAN lets one access port carry tagged frames from an IP phone in one VLAN and untagged frames from the attached PC in another. The native VLAN is the untagged VLAN of a trunk between switches. A private VLAN isolates hosts that share one VLAN from each other, and a management VLAN carries administrative access to the network devices themselves.

question: A company runs its web application on cloud virtual machines that its own staff maintain. It then moves the application to a platform as a service (PaaS) offering. Which task passes from the company to the provider as a result?
options: Managing access to the stored data
explanation: Under platform as a service the provider runs the operating system, runtime and middleware, so patching the operating system stops being the customer's job as it was on self-managed virtual machines. The physical servers are the provider's responsibility in both models, so that task does not move. Writing the application's code and managing access to its data stay with the customer in both models.

question: Two OSPF routers on one Ethernet link list each other as neighbors, but the adjacency stays in the ExStart state and never reaches Full. Which condition causes this?
options: Their interface MTU sizes are different.
Their OSPF area numbers are different.
explanation: An OSPF adjacency that stays in the ExStart state points to an MTU mismatch, because a router rejects database description packets that advertise a larger MTU than its own interface has. Routers with different area numbers, hello intervals or subnet masks reject each other's hello packets, so they never list each other as neighbors at all.

question: A payment processor can tolerate only a few minutes of downtime and almost no loss of transactions if its main data center is destroyed, and it accepts the cost of running duplicate systems. Which type of recovery site meets this requirement?
explanation: A hot site is a running duplicate of the production environment with its data kept current by replication, so it takes over within minutes at the highest cost of any recovery site. A warm site has equipment in place but needs its data restored, which takes hours. A cold site is empty space that has to be equipped first, which takes days or weeks, and a mobile site has to be delivered and set up before it is of use.

question: A technician reviews the counters on an access switch. Port 3 shows 318 CRC errors out of about 26 billion input packets since its counters were cleared 300 days ago. Port 17 shows 96 CRC errors out of about 19,000 input packets since its counters were cleared this morning. What should the technician conclude?
options: Port 3 has a fault, and port 17 is healthy
Neither port 3 nor port 17 has a fault
Port 17 has a fault, and port 3 is healthy
Both port 3 and port 17 have a fault to diagnose
explanation: An interface is judged by its error rate since the counters were cleared, not by its raw total. Port 3 has logged more errors, but 318 in about 26 billion packets is roughly one in 80 million, which is negligible, so it is healthy. Port 17 has 96 errors in about 19,000 packets, about one in 200, which points to a fault such as a damaged cable, interference or a duplex mismatch, and 19,000 packets are plenty to show a rate that high. About one CRC error a day over 300 days does not make a fault, and a rate of one in 200 is far too high to pass as normal.

question: A developer signs in to a cloud provider's web portal at midnight, picks three virtual servers from a catalog and has them running within minutes. Nobody at the provider reviews or approves the request. Which term describes this way of obtaining resources?
explanation: On-demand self-service means that a cloud customer obtains computing resources whenever they are needed, without any person at the provider having to act on the request. Zero-touch provisioning is a new network device downloading its own configuration when it is first connected. Infrastructure as code defines resources in version-controlled files instead of choosing them by hand in a portal, and rapid elasticity is capacity expanding and shrinking with demand.

question: A video recording server connects to its switch at 1 Gbps, and streams from 80 IP cameras reach that switch over 10 Gbps uplinks. Since the last 30 cameras were added, the recordings have short gaps, and the server's switch port shows output drops climbing while CRC errors, runts and giants stay at zero. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A damaged cable is corrupting frames on their way to the server
The uplinks are too slow to carry the video from the cameras
The server is sending frames larger than the port accepts
The video traffic exceeds the server port's capacity
explanation: Output drops count frames that a switch discards because a port's outbound queue is full, which happens when traffic arrives for that port faster than the port can send it. Video from 80 cameras arrives over the 10 Gbps uplinks faster than the 1 Gbps server port can send it, so the queue overflows and the dropped frames leave gaps in the recordings. A damaged cable shows up as CRC errors, oversized frames from the server would be counted as giants, which are input errors, and a congested uplink would drop frames at the switch that sends into it, not at the server's port.

question: An interface has the IPv6 address 2001:0db8:0000:00a0:0000:0000:0000:0100. Which is the shortest valid way to write this address?
explanation: IPv6 notation allows the leading zeros of each group to be dropped and one run of all-zero groups to be replaced by a double colon, which gives 2001:db8:0:a0::100. The form 2001:db8::a0::100 uses the double colon twice, which is not allowed because the address could no longer be expanded in one way. The form 2001:db8:0:a::1 drops trailing zeros, and 2001:db8::a0:100 moves the group a0, so both describe different addresses.

question: An optical power meter connected to the end of a fiber run reads 0 dBm. What does this reading mean?
options: One watt of light is reaching the meter
No measurable light is reaching the meter
Light is reaching the meter with no loss
One milliwatt of light is reaching the meter
explanation: The dBm scale expresses power relative to one milliwatt, so 0 dBm is exactly 1 mW, -10 dBm is 0.1 mW and -20 dBm is 0.01 mW. A run with no light would read a very low negative value or a low-signal warning, not 0 dBm, and one watt would be +30 dBm. Loss is the difference between the power sent and the power received, expressed in dB, so a single absolute reading in dBm cannot show that a run has no loss.

question: Routers in a small network send their entire routing tables to each directly connected neighbor every 30 seconds, so news of a failure takes minutes to reach every router. Which type of routing protocol behaves this way?
explanation: A distance-vector protocol such as RIP sends its whole routing table to its neighbors at regular intervals, so a change spreads one hop at a time and convergence is slow. A link-state protocol floods a change at once, and every router recalculates from a full map of the network. A path-vector protocol such as BGP sends updates only when routes change, and the hybrid label is given to EIGRP, which also sends partial updates.

question: Clients reach a web application at one address. A device at that address hands each new session to one of six web servers, tests their health and stops using any that fail the test. The servers' own addresses are not given to clients. Which technique is this?
explanation: A load balancer presents one virtual IP address to clients and hands each session to a healthy server in the pool behind it, so the servers' own addresses stay hidden and a failed server is skipped. Round-robin DNS spreads clients by returning the servers' addresses in turn and does not test their health. NIC teaming protects the links of a single server, and a first hop redundancy protocol shares a gateway address between routers.

question: A branch router fails and is replaced with an identical model. The engineer must return the site to service exactly as it was, with the same interface addresses, routes and access lists. Which configuration should be loaded onto the new router?
options: The baseline configuration for a new router
The backup configuration of the original router
The default configuration from the vendor
The production configuration of another site
explanation: A backup configuration is a saved copy of one device's own settings, kept so that the device or a replacement can be restored exactly from the most recent copy. The baseline, or golden, configuration is the approved template for new devices, and the vendor default is the factory starting point: neither holds the site's addresses or routes. The production configuration of another site would bring that site's addresses with it.

question: An IP phone is configured only with the domain example.com. It asks DNS for _sip._tcp.example.com and receives the host name and port number of the company's call server. Which record type returned this information?
explanation: An SRV record tells a client which host and port provide a named service, such as SIP over TCP, along with a priority and a weight. An MX record does this only for mail and carries no port. An NS record names a zone's authoritative servers, and an A record maps a host name to an IPv4 address.

question: A technician has gathered the symptoms of a fault and moves on to establish a theory of probable cause. What should the technician have when this step is complete?
options: A confirmed cause that is ready to be fixed
A likely explanation that is still to be tested
A list of actions and their potential effects
A written record of the fault and its resolution
explanation: A theory of probable cause is a reasoned explanation of the symptoms that has not yet been tested. The cause is confirmed only in the following step, when the theory is tested. A list of actions and their potential effects is the plan of action, which follows a confirmed theory, and the written record of the fault and its resolution is the documentation.

question: A camera at the far end of a warehouse drops off the network several times a day. A cable certifier reports that the twisted pair run from the switch to the camera is 138 m long and fails insertion loss, while its wire map and near-end crosstalk results pass. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A split pair somewhere along the cable run
Attenuation from a run longer than the standard allows
Interference from equipment along the cable route
Crosstalk from pairs untwisted too far at the wall jack
explanation: Insertion loss is the certifier's measure of attenuation, the weakening of a signal as it travels, and it grows with length; at 138 m the run is well past the 100 m channel limit for twisted pair, so the signal that reaches each end is at times too weak. The fix is to shorten the copper span, for example with a switch or a fiber link for part of the distance. Untwisted pairs and split pairs would fail the crosstalk or wire map tests, which passed, and interference adds noise rather than raising the cable's insertion loss.

question: A company requires that a remote worker's web browsing, as well as traffic to corporate servers, pass through the VPN so that the corporate firewall and web filter can inspect it. Which configuration meets this requirement?
explanation: A full tunnel sends all of a remote user's traffic, internet browsing included, through the VPN to the corporate network, where the company's firewall and filters can inspect it. A split tunnel sends only corporate traffic through the VPN, split DNS sends only internal name lookups to the company's DNS servers, and a clientless VPN reaches web applications through a browser without carrying the device's other traffic.

question: As a web request travels from a browser down toward the network adapter, the OSI layers along the way encapsulate it. What does a layer do when it encapsulates?
options: Rebuilds the data from smaller pieces
Adds its own header to the data
Removes its own header from the data
Splits the data into smaller pieces
explanation: Encapsulation is the step in which a layer adds its own header, and at the Data Link layer also a trailer, to the data handed down from the layer above. Removing a header is decapsulation, which happens as data moves up the stack on the receiving host. Splitting data into smaller pieces is segmentation, which is a separate task of the Transport layer, and rebuilding the data is the matching task on the receiving host.

question: A technician installs a cable modem in a home. Which cable and connector type join the modem to the provider's wall outlet?
options: Cat 3 telephone cable with RJ11 connectors
RG-6 coaxial cable with F-type connectors
RG-58 coaxial cable with BNC connectors
Cat 6 UTP cable with RJ45 connectors
explanation: Cable broadband and cable television arrive on 75-ohm RG-6 coaxial cable, which ends in screw-on F-type connectors. RG-58 with BNC connectors is the 50-ohm coaxial cable of old 10BASE2 Ethernet. Cat 6 with RJ45 connectors joins the modem to a router or computer on the LAN side, and Cat 3 telephone cable with RJ11 connectors carries the telephone line that a DSL modem uses.

question: Every IPv6 interface automatically creates a unicast address that is valid only on its own segment and that routers never forward. With which prefix does that address begin?
explanation: Link-local addresses use the prefix FE80::/10, and every IPv6 interface creates one for itself for neighbor discovery and other traffic that stays on a single segment. FC00::/7 is the unique local range, which is routed inside an organization but not on the internet. FF00::/8 is the multicast range. FEC0::/10 was the site-local prefix, which has been retired in favor of unique local addresses.

question: While waiting in a hallway, a visitor watches an engineer type the code into the server room's keypad, and the room is later entered with that code. Which social engineering technique did the visitor use?
explanation: Shoulder surfing is watching someone enter a code, a password or a PIN, from close by or through a camera or binoculars, in order to use it later. Tailgating is following an authorized person through a door before it closes, dumpster diving is searching discarded papers and equipment for information, and phishing uses fraudulent messages to trick people into giving information away.

question: A utility installs flow sensors along 200 km of rural pipeline, far from any building. Each sensor sends a small reading to headquarters every hour over licensed spectrum that a carrier operates. Which wireless technology fits?
explanation: Cellular networks (LTE and 5G) use licensed spectrum and carrier towers to reach devices spread over many kilometers, which suits remote sensors that have no local network. Bluetooth reaches roughly 10 meters, and Zigbee and Z-Wave are low-power mesh protocols for one building, where each node must be within tens of meters of the next.

question: An unlabeled copper cable leaves a wall plate and disappears into the ceiling. A technician must follow it to find which patch panel port it reaches. Which tool should be used?
explanation: A tone generator places an audible signal on a cable, and its matching inductive probe picks up that tone through the jacket, so the cable can be followed through walls and found among the ports of a patch panel. A loopback plug tests whether a port can send and receive, a multimeter checks continuity once both ends are known, and a light meter measures optical power on fiber.

question: A provider's SLA guarantees 99.9 percent uptime, measured over a 365-day year. About how much downtime in a year does the guarantee allow?
explanation: An uptime of 99.9 percent leaves 0.1 percent of the year for downtime, and 0.001 of 8,760 hours is 8.76 hours. The 52.6 minutes belong to 99.99 percent, where the allowance is ten times smaller. The 43.8 hours belong to 99.5 percent, and the 87.6 hours belong to 99 percent.

question: A host builds its own IPv6 address with SLAAC and uses EUI-64 for the last 64 bits. From which value does EUI-64 derive that part of the address?
options: The output of a random number generator
The MAC address of its own interface
The link-local address of the router
The client identifier used for DHCPv6
explanation: EUI-64 builds the 64-bit interface identifier from the 48-bit MAC address: it inserts FFFE in the middle and inverts the seventh bit of the first byte. The link-local address of the router is what the host uses as its default gateway. The DHCPv6 client identifier names the host to a DHCPv6 server and does not form part of an address. A random number is what privacy extensions use instead of EUI-64, so that the address does not reveal the hardware.

question: A security administrator needs a weekly report that lists every server with missing patches or weak settings and matches each finding to a published CVE entry. Which tool produces this report?
explanation: A vulnerability scanner probes each host and compares what it finds with a database of known weaknesses, so it can report missing patches and poor settings by CVE entry. A port scanner stops at listing which ports are open. A protocol analyzer decodes captured packets, and a NetFlow collector records which hosts exchanged traffic and how much.

question: A company will move into a building that is still under construction, so no radio measurements can be taken there yet. The wireless engineer loads the floor plans and wall materials into planning software to estimate where access points should go. Which type of site survey is this?
explanation: A predictive survey models radio coverage in software from the floor plans, the building materials and the access point specifications, so it needs no measurements on site. A passive survey walks the site and records the signals that are already on the air, and an active survey connects to an access point to measure throughput and loss. A validation survey is done after installation to confirm that the design was met.

question: A Cisco router records this message: %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to down. Which syslog severity does the message have?
explanation: In a Cisco log message the number between the facility name and the mnemonic is the syslog severity, so LINK-3-UPDOWN is severity 3, which is named Error. Critical is severity 2 and Alert is severity 1, both more urgent than the loss of one interface. Warning is severity 4, one step less severe than Error.

question: A server takes about 30 seconds to gain network access each time it restarts, and its DHCP request times out. The administrator enables PortFast on the switch port of the server. What does PortFast change?
options: The port stops sending BPDUs and ignores those it receives
The port moves straight to forwarding when its link comes up
The port is disabled when it receives a spanning tree BPDU
The port is prevented from becoming the root port of the switch
explanation: PortFast puts an access port into the forwarding state as soon as its link comes up, skipping the listening and learning delay of about 30 seconds. Disabling a port that receives a BPDU is the work of BPDU guard, which is normally paired with PortFast. Preventing a port from becoming the root port is root guard, and suppressing BPDUs in both directions is BPDU filter.

question: A company's lab team will run DNS for lab.example.com on its own two servers. Which record type must be added to the example.com zone so that queries for names under lab.example.com are referred to those servers?
explanation: NS records name the servers that are authoritative for a zone, and NS records for a subdomain placed in the parent zone delegate that subdomain to the servers they name. The SOA record holds a zone's own primary server, serial number and timers and does not refer queries elsewhere. A PTR record maps an address to a name, and a CNAME record makes a single name an alias of another.

question: A technician has confirmed that a core switch needs a firmware upgrade. Before touching the switch, the technician works out which users and services the upgrade will interrupt. Which step of the troubleshooting methodology is the technician carrying out?
options: Test the theory to determine the cause
explanation: Identifying the potential effects of a solution is part of establishing the plan of action, before anything is changed. The theory was tested earlier, when the need for the upgrade was confirmed. Implementing the solution is the upgrade itself, and verifying full system functionality is the check that is made once the upgrade is complete.

question: Unlike SNMPv1, SNMPv2c can carry 64-bit values in its messages. Which SNMPv1 problem does this solve?
options: Walks that need a new request for each object
Counters that wrap around too soon on fast links
Polls that cross the network without encryption
Traps that are lost without any acknowledgment
explanation: A 32-bit counter of octets can wrap around within seconds on a 10 Gbps link, so SNMPv2c added 64-bit counters that last far longer between polls. The same version added the Inform, a notification that the manager acknowledges, and GetBulk, which returns many objects in a single request. Encryption of SNMP messages came later, with the privacy option of SNMPv3.

question: A designer mounts an access point with a patch antenna flat against the end wall of a lecture hall. Which coverage pattern should the designer expect from this antenna?
options: A narrow beam aimed at one distant point
A wide beam toward one side of the antenna
Two beams in opposite directions along one axis
An even ring of signal around the antenna
explanation: A patch antenna is a flat directional antenna that radiates a wide beam from its face, so it covers the area in front of the wall it is mounted on. A narrow beam aimed at one distant point is produced by a parabolic dish or a Yagi, and an even ring of signal in the horizontal plane is the pattern of an omnidirectional antenna. Two opposite beams come from a bidirectional antenna, which is used along corridors and tunnels.

question: Two offices are joined by a satellite link. Voice calls sound clear and steady, but there is a constant pause of more than half a second before each reply is heard, so people talk over each other. Which condition causes this?
explanation: Latency is the time a packet takes to cross the network, and a satellite path adds a long but constant delay, so speech is clear yet late. Jitter is variation in that delay, which makes audio choppy, and packet loss removes pieces of the speech. Low bandwidth causes congestion, which shows up as jitter and loss, not as a steady pause.

question: A router recalculates its paths with Dijkstra's algorithm each time the network topology changes. Which routing protocol is the router running?
explanation: OSPF runs Dijkstra's shortest path first algorithm on its link-state database to calculate the lowest-cost path to every network. EIGRP uses the Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL), and RIP relies on the Bellman-Ford algorithm. BGP uses neither: it chooses among paths by comparing their attributes.

question: A small office router has no routing protocol enabled. To reach the 10.20.0.0/24 network behind a second router, the administrator types in the destination prefix and the next-hop address. Which type of route has been created?
explanation: A static route is one that an administrator enters by hand, and it stays in place until it is changed or removed. A connected route is added automatically for a network attached to one of the router's own interfaces. A default route matches every destination and a summary route covers several networks with one entry, so neither describes a route to the single prefix 10.20.0.0/24.

question: A technician terminates both ends of a cable in the same nonstandard order, placing each color pair on two neighboring pins: 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6, and 7 and 8. A basic continuity tester shows all eight pins connected straight through, yet the link to a 100 Mbps camera logs constant errors. What is the fault?
options: A shorted pair: two wires that carry different signals touch
A split pair: one signal is carried on wires of two different pairs
An open pair: one wire of a signal pair has no end-to-end path
A reversed pair: the two wires of one pair swap pins at one end
explanation: 100BASE-TX carries one direction of traffic on pins 1 and 2 and the other direction on pins 3 and 6, and each of those signal pairs must be one twisted pair so that noise cancels. Placing the colors on neighboring pins puts pins 3 and 6 on two different twisted pairs, a split pair, which causes heavy crosstalk and errors even though every pin reaches the same pin at the far end, which is all a basic continuity tester checks. An open or a short would fail that continuity test, and a reversed pair would show up on it as crossed pins.

question: A network team adds a configuration monitoring tool to its management platform. Which problem is this tool designed to report?
options: A router that is missing a patch for a published weakness
A switch that runs settings different from the approved copy
A laptop that joins the network with its antivirus turned off
A host that sends traffic that matches a known attack signature
explanation: Configuration monitoring compares the settings each device is running with an approved baseline copy and reports any difference, which is often called drift. A missing patch for a published weakness is found by a vulnerability scanner. A laptop with its antivirus turned off is stopped by a network access control posture check, and traffic that matches an attack signature is reported by an intrusion detection system.

question: A university owns the fiber that joins its 14 buildings, which stand on one site about 3 km across. The network does not extend beyond the university grounds. Which network type is this?
explanation: A campus area network (CAN) joins the buildings of one organization on a single site, over cabling that the organization owns. A MAN spans a whole city and usually belongs to a provider, a WAN joins sites in different cities or countries over carrier circuits, and a WLAN is a local network that devices join by radio.

question: A hosted email provider asks a company to prove control of example.com by publishing a verification string, and to publish a list of the servers allowed to send mail for the domain. Which record type holds both items?
explanation: A TXT record holds free text, which is how a domain publishes verification strings and its SPF policy, the list of servers allowed to send its mail. An MX record names the servers that receive mail for the domain, not those allowed to send it. An SRV record gives the host and port of a service, and a PTR record maps an address back to a name.

question: A switch interface in a conference room should accept frames from no more than three source MAC addresses and shut itself down if a fourth appears. Which feature should be configured on that interface?
explanation: Port security caps the number of source MAC addresses an interface will learn and can shut the interface down when one more appears, which also blunts MAC flooding. DHCP snooping blocks DHCP server replies on untrusted ports, BPDU guard disables a port that receives spanning tree frames from another switch, and 802.1X makes each device authenticate before the port forwards its traffic.

question: A data center is rebuilt as a spine and leaf fabric. Which links between devices does this design call for?
options: Each leaf switch to every other leaf switch
Each spine switch to the other spines
Each server to two spine switches
Each leaf switch to every spine switch
explanation: In a spine and leaf fabric every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, and that is the only switch-to-switch cabling, so traffic between any two leaf switches crosses exactly one spine. Leaf switches do not connect to one another, spine switches do not connect to one another, and servers attach to leaf switches, not directly to the spine.

question: A user's PC cannot open files on a server. Using divide and conquer, a technician starts at the network layer and pings the server's IP address from the PC. The ping fails, but other PCs on the same subnet can ping the server. Where should the technician focus NEXT?
options: The layers above the one just tested, starting with the server's file-sharing service
The layer just tested and those below it, starting with this PC and its connection
The application layer first, then each layer below it until the fault appears
The physical layer of another PC on the same subnet, then each layer above it in turn
explanation: In divide and conquer, a test at a middle layer decides the direction: a failed test points to that layer and the layers below it, while a passed test points up the stack. Other PCs on the same subnet can ping the server, so the server and the shared path are working, which points to this PC's addressing, switch port or cable. Moving up to the file-sharing service ignores the failed ping, restarting from the application layer abandons the method, and the other PCs have already shown that their own lower layers work.

question: To stop CRC errors on a link that runs past large motors, a factory replaced a UTP run with shielded twisted pair, but the errors did not improve. The technician finds that the new cable was terminated with ordinary unshielded jacks and plugs at both ends. What is the MOST likely reason the errors continue?
options: Shielded cable adds enough attenuation to cause errors by itself
Shielding stops crosstalk inside a cable but not outside noise
A shield must be bonded to ground to drain away noise
Shielded cable needs a crossover at one end to carry Ethernet
explanation: A cable shield works only when it is continuous through shielded connectors and bonded to ground, so that noise induced in it is carried away instead of reaching the pairs. Terminated with unshielded jacks and plugs, the shield is left floating, gives little protection and can even pick up and pass on noise. Shielding exists to keep outside interference out, a properly installed shielded cable does not weaken the signal enough to cause errors, and shielding has nothing to do with whether a cable is wired straight-through or crossover.

question: A cafe's guest wireless network has a /24 DHCP scope that hands out each address for eight days. Most guests stay less than an hour, about 60 are present at any time, and new guests now receive no address. Which change corrects the cause?
options: Enable DHCP snooping on the switches
Move the guests to a larger subnet
Add an exclusion range to the scope
explanation: When clients come and go quickly, a long lease keeps each address tied to a device that has already left, so a shorter lease returns addresses to the pool in time for new clients. A larger subnet is the fix when more devices are present at once than the scope can hold, which is not the case with 60 guests in a /24. DHCP snooping blocks rogue DHCP servers, and an exclusion range would shrink the pool further.

question: An administrator sets the port that faces a neighboring switch to trunk mode. What does a port in that mode do?
options: Supplies power to a device over the data cable
Carries frames for several VLANs over a single link
Connects one end device to a single assigned VLAN
Receives copies of the frames seen on other ports
explanation: A trunk port carries the frames of several VLANs over one link, using IEEE 802.1Q tags so that the switch at the other end knows which VLAN each frame belongs to. Connecting one end device to a single VLAN is the job of an access port. Receiving copies of frames from other ports is what a mirror port does for a protocol analyzer, and supplying power over the data cable is Power over Ethernet.

question: A phone streams music to wireless earbuds and sends alerts to a smartwatch over Bluetooth, all within about two meters of their owner. Which network type do these devices form?
explanation: A personal area network (PAN) links the devices around one person over a few meters, and Bluetooth is its most common technology. A LAN serves a room, floor or building through switches, a WLAN does the same over Wi-Fi access points, and a MAN spans a city.

question: An attacker sends small DNS queries to thousands of open resolvers with the victim's address forged as the source, so that each resolver sends the victim a reply many times larger than the query. Which attack is this?
explanation: DNS amplification uses open resolvers as reflectors, so that small queries carrying a forged source address make them send far larger replies to the victim. DNS cache poisoning plants false records in a resolver, DNS tunneling hides other traffic inside DNS messages, and DNS hijacking changes which server or records a victim's lookups reach.

question: Sensors in a server room raise an alert when relative humidity falls below 40 percent or rises above 60 percent. Which risk to the equipment does the lower limit guard against?
explanation: Dry air lets static charge build up on people and surfaces, so low relative humidity raises the risk of electrostatic discharge into sensitive components. Condensation and corrosion are the dangers of high humidity, which is what the upper limit guards against. Overheating depends on temperature and airflow, and a temperature sensor watches for it.

question: Users report choppy audio on VoIP calls. A monitor shows an average one-way delay of 45 ms, 0.2 percent of packets lost, and arrival times that vary by up to 70 ms between packets. Which condition explains the poor audio?
explanation: Jitter is variation in packet arrival times, and swings of 70 ms are more than a typical jitter buffer can absorb, so voice breaks up; for VoIP it should stay under about 30 ms. A one-way delay of 45 ms is well inside the usual 150 ms limit, 0.2 percent loss is under the 1 percent guideline, and a codec mismatch stops calls from connecting rather than making them choppy.

question: An online ticket seller's cloud platform adds web servers by itself in the minutes after a concert goes on sale and removes them again once the queue clears. Which cloud characteristic does this behavior show?
explanation: Rapid elasticity is the automatic expansion and release of capacity as demand rises and falls, so the customer does not hold idle servers for long. Scalability is the ability to grow to meet a larger load, but the term does not cover releasing that capacity automatically afterward. Measured service is the metering of what each customer consumes, and multitenancy is many customers sharing the same infrastructure.

question: An old lab network consists of one length of coaxial cable that runs past every computer. Each computer attaches to it with a T-connector, and a 50-ohm resistor caps each end of the cable. Which topology is this?
explanation: A bus topology attaches every device to one shared backbone cable that is terminated at both ends, as in early coaxial Ethernet. A star gives each device its own cable to a central switch, a ring joins each device to two neighbors in a closed loop with no ends to terminate, and a mesh gives devices direct links to several others.

question: A technician re-terminates a wall jack from T568A to T568B. Which two wire pairs stay on the same pins?
explanation: T568A and T568B differ in the positions of the green and orange pairs, which trade places on pins 1, 2, 3 and 6. The blue pair stays on pins 4 and 5 and the brown pair on pins 7 and 8 in both standards. Orange and green are the two pairs that move, so any answer that names one of them is wrong.

question: A branch office manager who has never used a command line must change the guest Wi-Fi passphrase on the office's access point every month. Which connection method should the manager use?
explanation: A graphical user interface, usually a web page that the device serves, lets a person change settings by clicking through menus and forms, so it suits someone who has never used a command line. SSH and a console cable both lead to the device's command line, one over the network and one over a serial link, and a REST API is built for scripts and management software rather than for a person.

question: Two RIP routers in a routing loop keep advertising a failed network back to each other, raising its metric each time. Which loop-prevention mechanism limits how far the metric can climb, so that the network is declared unreachable at 16?
explanation: RIP treats a hop count of 16 as unreachable, so the maximum hop count of 15 puts an end to counting to infinity and limits the size of a RIP network. Split horizon stops a router from advertising a route back out of the interface it was learned on. Route poisoning advertises a failed route as unreachable at once, and a hold-down timer makes a router ignore new information about a failed route for a set time.

question: A data center administrator wants to graph the internal temperature of every switch and to be alerted when a reading passes a safe limit. Which method collects these readings?
options: SNMP polling from a management station
ICMP echo requests from a test host
Flow export to a traffic collector
Port mirroring to a packet analyzer
explanation: Switches publish the readings of their temperature sensors as SNMP objects, so a management station can poll them on a schedule, graph the values and raise an alert when a threshold is passed. Flow export describes the traffic that crosses a device, and port mirroring copies frames to an analyzer, so neither carries sensor readings. ICMP echo requests show only whether a device answers and how quickly.

question: A data center team is choosing copper cabling for its switch-to-server links and is considering Cat 8. What is the highest speed that Cat 8 is rated for, and over what distance?
explanation: Cat 8 is rated for 40 Gbps (40GBASE-T) over a channel of 30 meters, which suits links between switches and servers in the same or a neighboring rack. Cat 6a is the category rated for 10 Gbps over 100 meters, and Cat 6 carries 10 Gbps to about 55 meters. Cat 5e is rated for 1 Gbps over 100 meters.

question: Users on one switch port report slow transfers. From the Cisco switch's command line, a technician wants to see that port's speed, duplex setting and counters for CRC errors and collisions. Which command shows these?
explanation: On a Cisco switch, show interfaces reports each port's status, speed and duplex along with its error counters, such as CRC errors, runts and collisions. The command show mac address-table lists the MAC addresses learned on each port, show vlan brief lists the VLANs and their access ports, and show ip route displays the routing table.

question: Some clients on a VLAN receive addresses in 192.168.0.0/24 with a gateway of 192.168.0.1, a range the company does not use anywhere. The company's scope for that VLAN still has free leases. What is the most likely cause?
options: A missing IP helper on the VLAN's router
A wrong router option in the company's scope
A rogue DHCP server on the VLAN
An incorrect VLAN on the client switch ports
explanation: An unauthorized DHCP server, such as a home router plugged into a wall jack, answers some clients before the real server does and hands them its own range and gateway; DHCP snooping on the switches blocks such servers. A wrong router option would give clients the correct range with the wrong gateway, a missing IP helper leaves remote clients with APIPA addresses, and a port in the wrong VLAN gets an address from another company range.

question: A badge system logs the time, the door and the badge number for every attempt to open a secure door, whether it is granted or denied. What security benefit does this log provide?
options: Proof that the badge holder is present
An audit trail for incident investigations
A picture of each person at the door
A barrier against entry without a badge
explanation: A badge access log is an audit trail: it shows which badge was used at which door and when, including denied attempts, and investigators can match it against camera footage after an incident. Blocking entry without a badge is the job of the locked door and its reader, proving that the cardholder is the person at the door takes a second factor such as a biometric, and a picture of each person comes from a camera.

question: After hours, a sensor in a data center hallway raises an alarm when the infrared energy in its field of view changes, as it does when a person's body heat enters it. Which detection method is this?
explanation: Motion detection with a passive infrared sensor notices the change in heat as a person moves through its view and raises an alarm, which suits areas that should be empty. Tamper detection shows that a device or case was opened, asset tracking records where each piece of equipment is and who has it, and CCTV recording captures images for later review.

question: After server01 moves to a new IP address, a technician runs nslookup server01.example.com on an affected computer and receives the new address. However, applications on that computer still connect to the old address. What is the most likely cause?
options: An expired DHCP lease on server01
A stale entry in the local DNS cache
A missing PTR record for the new address
An outdated A record on the DNS server
explanation: Applications resolve names through the computer's local DNS cache, which can hold an old address until the entry expires, while nslookup sends its query straight to the DNS server and skips that cache. Flushing the cache with ipconfig /flushdns on Windows fixes it at once. An outdated A record on the server would make nslookup return the old address too, a missing PTR record affects only reverse lookups, and a DHCP lease on server01 does not change what the client has cached.

question: In a three-tier campus network, the wiring-closet switches on every floor uplink to a pair of multilayer switches, which route between VLANs and apply filtering policy before traffic reaches the backbone. At which layer does that pair of switches sit?
explanation: The distribution layer sits between the access layer and the core, where it aggregates the uplinks of the access switches, routes between VLANs and applies policy. The access layer is where end devices plug in, and the core layer is the fast backbone that the distribution switches feed. A spine layer belongs to a spine-and-leaf data center fabric, not to the three-tier model.

question: A network engineer adds statements to a router interface that permit traffic from two partner IP addresses to an internal server on TCP port 443 and drop all other traffic. What is the engineer configuring?
explanation: An access control list is an ordered set of permit and deny statements that a router or firewall applies to traffic by address, protocol and port, ending in an implicit deny for anything not matched. URL filtering blocks requests by web address, content filtering blocks by the category or content of what is requested, and port forwarding maps an outside port to an inside host without limiting who may connect.

question: After SSID broadcast is disabled on an access point, which frames can a wireless analyzer still capture to learn the network's name?
explanation: A client joining a hidden network names it in clear text in its probe requests and association requests, and the access point repeats the name in its probe responses, so an analyzer learns it the next time any client connects. Beacons from a hidden network keep going out but leave the name field blank, and deauthentication and disassociation frames carry only a reason code, though attackers send them to force clients to reconnect and reveal the name.

question: A database application drops its sessions several times a day. An engineer needs to see which host sends the TCP reset and what the two hosts exchanged just before it. Which data should the engineer collect?
explanation: Packet captures record every segment with its flags and payload, so they show which host sent the reset and the exchange that led up to it. NetFlow records summarize each conversation by addresses, ports and volume without the packets themselves. Syslog messages report events that a device chose to log, and interface counters give only totals of traffic and errors on a port.

question: An office needs 10GBASE-T at every desk, and several horizontal runs are 85 meters long. What is the lowest category of twisted-pair cable that is rated for these runs?
explanation: Cat 6a is the lowest category rated to carry 10GBASE-T over a full 100-meter channel. Cat 6 carries 10GBASE-T to about 55 meters, so it falls short on an 85-meter run, and Cat 5e is rated for 1 Gbps. Cat 7 also carries 10 Gbps over 100 meters, but it is a higher category than these runs require.

question: A Linux server must send packets for 10.50.0.0/16 through a second gateway instead of its default gateway. Which command adds the required entry to the kernel's table and can also display that table?
explanation: The ip route command displays the Linux routing table and adds or removes entries, for example ip route add 10.50.0.0/16 via 10.1.1.254. The ip address command assigns and shows interface addresses, ip link brings interfaces up or down and shows their hardware settings, and ip neigh shows the neighbor table of IP-to-MAC mappings. The older route command does the same job as ip route.

question: A packet capture taken while an IP phone starts up shows the phone exchanging data with a server on UDP port 69. Which protocol is the phone using?
explanation: TFTP uses UDP port 69 and is a simple way to fetch files such as phone configurations, switch images and network boot files, with no login and no encryption. DHCP uses the neighboring UDP ports 67 and 68 to hand out addresses. SNMP uses UDP ports 161 and 162 for monitoring. DNS uses port 53 to resolve names.

question: An administrator changes an A record in a zone file on the primary DNS server and reloads the zone. A day later the secondary server still gives the old address in its authoritative answers. Which step did the administrator MOST likely omit?
options: Add an NS record for the secondary server
Lower the TTL value on the changed record
Increase the serial number in the SOA record
Clear the cache on the secondary server
explanation: A secondary server copies a zone only when the serial number in the primary's SOA record is higher than the one it already holds, so a change made without raising the serial never reaches it. A lower TTL shortens how long resolvers cache an answer but does not update a secondary's copy of the zone. An NS record lists a server as authoritative, and clearing a cache affects only records learned from other servers.

question: Clients on an access VLAN are receiving addresses from a home router that someone connected to a wall jack. Which switch feature stops this by dropping address offers that arrive on untrusted ports?
explanation: DHCP snooping treats ports as untrusted unless they are configured otherwise and drops DHCP offers and acknowledgments that arrive on them, which shuts out a rogue DHCP server. Dynamic ARP inspection also relies on trusted ports but checks ARP messages, port security limits the MAC addresses a port may learn, and 802.1X makes a device authenticate before the port forwards its traffic.

question: An auditor's account is given read access to the firewall logs and to nothing else, because reading logs is all that the audit requires. Which security principle does this follow?
explanation: Least privilege gives an account the permissions its task needs and nothing beyond them, which limits the damage if the account is misused. Defense in depth is the use of several different layers of control. Separation of duties divides one sensitive task between people so that no single person can carry it out alone. Zero trust verifies each request instead of trusting a device for being on the internal network.

question: A law firm pays a monthly fee per user for an email and document suite that staff open in a web browser. The firm runs no servers for it, and the vendor patches and upgrades the suite. Which service model is the firm using?
explanation: Software as a service delivers a finished application that the provider hosts, patches and upgrades, so the customer only uses it, usually through a browser. Platform as a service is for customers who deploy their own code on a managed platform, and infrastructure as a service rents out virtual servers that the customer must manage. Desktop as a service delivers a whole virtual desktop, not a single application suite.

question: A contractor finishing a Cat 6A installation is told that a basic cable tester is not enough and a certifier is required. What does the certifier check that the basic tester does not?
options: Where a cable runs through the walls
Loss and crosstalk against the standard
The wiring order of the pins at each end
Continuity of each conductor from end to end
explanation: A certifier measures loss, crosstalk and return loss across the frequency range of the cable's category and compares the results with the standard's limits. That pass or fail record is what installers hand over for warranties, while continuity and pin order are already checked by a basic tester, and following a cable inside walls is the job of a tone generator and probe.

question: A technician must take graphical control of Linux and macOS desktops from a Windows laptop, using a platform-independent protocol that listens on TCP port 5900 by default. Which protocol should the technician use?
explanation: VNC is a platform-independent graphical remote desktop protocol that listens on TCP port 5900 by default, and it should run through SSH or a VPN when the server does not encrypt the session. RDP is the Microsoft graphical protocol on TCP port 3389, while SSH on port 22 and Telnet on port 23 give command-line access rather than a desktop.

question: A technician runs nslookup www.example.com against the company's internal DNS server, and the address is shown under the heading Non-authoritative answer. What does this heading say about the internal server?
options: It followed a CNAME to the address
It is a secondary server for the example.com zone
It does not host the zone for example.com
It failed to validate the DNSSEC signature
explanation: A non-authoritative answer comes from a server that does not host the zone and is passing on what it learned from other servers, often from its cache. A secondary server holds a full copy of the zone, so its answers are authoritative just as the primary's are. A failed DNSSEC validation returns an error instead of an address, and nslookup lists an alias on its own line whichever server answers.

question: A network diagram labels one part of an office network as the WLAN. Which statement describes that part?
options: A carrier network that devices join over cellular radio
A local network that devices join over Wi-Fi
A logical network that a switch builds from chosen ports
A personal network that spans a few meters
explanation: A WLAN is a wireless local area network: it covers the same local area as a cabled LAN, but devices join it over Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11) through access points. A carrier network reached over cellular radio is a wireless WAN, a network of a few meters around one person is a PAN, and a logical network built from chosen switch ports is a VLAN.

question: A company approves one standard set of router settings, including security hardening, SNMP and NTP servers. Every new router must be built from it, and audits compare installed routers against it. What is this approved reference called?
explanation: A baseline configuration, also called a golden configuration, is the approved standard that new devices are built from and that audits measure existing devices against. On many devices the running configuration is the set of settings active in memory and the startup configuration is the saved copy loaded at boot. A backup configuration is a stored copy of one device's settings, kept for restoring that device.

question: Before access points are installed in a new warehouse, an engineer walks the building and measures signal strength, channel use and sources of interference. Which document records the results?
explanation: A site survey report records the radio measurements taken in a building, such as signal strength, channel use and interference, and it guides where the access points go. A baseline configuration is the approved standard of device settings. A wiring diagram records cable runs and their ports, and a floor plan shows the rooms and closets but none of the measurements.

question: Wireless clients in one office keep dropping off the network. A capture shows a stream of forged 802.11 management frames, apparently sent by the access point, telling each client to leave. Which attack is this?
explanation: A deauthentication attack forges management frames in the access point's name to disconnect clients, and protected management frames, which WPA3 requires, defend against it. Jamming disrupts the channel with radio noise rather than frames, an evil twin lures clients to a fake access point, and a SYN flood fills a server's queue of half-open TCP connections.

question: In a shared office building, a visitor gets an incorrect password error on the guest Wi-Fi, even when the technician types the passphrase from reception for her. Other visitors connect with the same passphrase. What should the technician check?
options: Whether the AP has reached its client limit
Whether she chose the right network name
Whether her device has a static IP address
Whether the guest DHCP scope has free addresses
explanation: In a building shared with other tenants, an incorrect password error with a passphrase that works for everyone else usually means the visitor picked a neighbor's network with a similar name and a different passphrase. Address problems such as a full scope or a static address arise only after the password is accepted, and an AP at its client limit refuses the association rather than the password.

question: A Layer 3 switch carries VLAN 10 and VLAN 20. Hosts in each VLAN must use an address on that switch as their default gateway, so that it routes between the two VLANs. What should the administrator configure for each VLAN?
options: A switch port in trunk mode
explanation: A switch virtual interface (SVI) is a logical Layer 3 interface for one VLAN on a multilayer switch, and its IP address serves as that VLAN's default gateway, so the switch routes between VLANs. A router subinterface does the same job on a router reached over a trunk, a trunk port only carries the VLANs between devices, and a loopback interface belongs to no VLAN.

question: A provider assigns a customer the block 203.0.113.8/29 for its public servers. How many usable host addresses does this block contain?
explanation: A /29 leaves three host bits, which gives eight addresses, and two of them (the network address and the broadcast address) cannot be given to hosts, so six are usable. Eight is the size of the whole block before those two are removed. Fourteen is the usable count of a /28, and two is the usable count of a /30, the size often used for a link between two routers.

question: A firewall's reporting tool queries DNS with each source IP address so that its reports can show host names. For the internal servers the tool finds no names, although their names resolve to the correct addresses. Which record type is missing for these servers?
explanation: A PTR record maps an IP address back to a host name and lives in a reverse lookup zone, which is what a tool uses when it starts with an address and wants a name. An A record does the opposite, mapping a name to an IPv4 address, so it can exist without any PTR record. A CNAME record makes one name an alias of another, and an NS record names the servers that are authoritative for a zone.

question: A 10 Gbps fiber uplink between two switches shows a steadily rising count of CRC errors on one end, while the other end shows none. What is the most likely cause?
options: Dirty connector on the patch cord
MTU mismatch between the two switches
Duplex mismatch at the two ends
explanation: CRC errors mean that frames arrive corrupted, and on a fiber link the usual reason is a dirty or damaged connector, or a failing transceiver, on the receiving side. Light in a fiber is not affected by electrical interference, a 10 Gbps link runs only at full duplex so a duplex mismatch cannot occur, and an MTU mismatch causes oversized frames to be dropped rather than corrupted.

question: A switch port shows no link to a desk computer, so a technician connects a loopback plug to the port. What does the plug check?
options: Whether the port supplies PoE power
Whether the port transmits and receives
Whether the cable has an open or a short
Which wall jack the cable reaches
explanation: A loopback plug wires a port's transmit pins back to its receive pins, so the port hears its own signal and shows whether its transmit and receive circuits work with the cabling taken out of the test. A PoE tester checks whether a port supplies power, a cable tester finds opens and shorts in a run, and a tone generator with its probe finds which wall jack a cable reaches.

question: An attacker telephones an employee, claims to be from the IT help desk and talks the employee into reading out their password. Which attack is this?
explanation: Vishing is social engineering by telephone, in which a caller poses as someone trusted to talk the victim into giving up information. Smishing delivers the lure by text message, tailgating is following an authorized person through a secured door, and shoulder surfing is watching someone type a password or PIN.

question: A network team wants every command an administrator enters on a router to be authorized by a central server, with the entire exchange between router and server encrypted and carried over TCP. Which protocol meets these needs?
explanation: TACACS+ runs over TCP port 49, encrypts the whole body of each packet and handles authorization separately from authentication, which lets a server approve or refuse individual commands. RADIUS runs over UDP, hides only the password and returns authorization together with authentication. LDAP queries a directory of accounts. SSH encrypts the administrator's own session to the router, but it is not an AAA protocol.

question: A security team adds a honeypot to the VLAN that holds its file servers. What is the role of this system?
options: It inspects network traffic for attack signatures
It forwards requests on behalf of its clients
It poses as a valuable target to attract attackers
It relays administrator sessions into the VLAN
explanation: A honeypot is a decoy: it looks like a real target, holds nothing of value and is watched, so any connection to it points to an intruder. Inspecting traffic for attack signatures is the work of an intrusion detection system. Relaying administrator sessions into a protected network is the job of a jump server. Forwarding requests on behalf of clients is what a proxy server does.

question: Twice this year, a badge was stolen from an employee's car, and the thief used it to enter the data center before the theft was reported. Which change would stop a stolen badge from opening the door on its own?
options: Disable badges once they are reported lost
Log each badge swipe at the door
Require a PIN with each badge
Add a camera that records the door
explanation: Requiring a PIN as well as the badge makes entry depend on something the person knows as well as something the person has, so a stolen badge alone no longer opens the door. Logging badge swipes and recording the door show who entered only after the fact, and disabling a badge once it is reported lost does nothing in the hours before anyone notices the theft.

question: A network administrator finds that a switch is sending some unicast frames out of all the other ports in VLAN 30 instead of one port. Which condition in the MAC address table makes a switch treat a unicast frame this way?
options: Its table lists the destination address on the arrival port
Its table has no entry for the destination address
Its table has no entry for the source address
Its table lists the source address on a different port
explanation: A switch floods a unicast frame out of every port in the VLAN, except the one it arrived on, when the destination address has no entry in its MAC address table. An unknown source address only causes the switch to learn it. A destination on the arrival port means that the frame is filtered, because the target is on the segment it came from, and a source seen on a different port makes the switch update its entry.

question: A technician unplugs each fiber patch cord on a switch to label it and plugs it back into the same port. Afterward, one 10 Gbps link starts logging CRC errors, and its receive power has fallen from -3.2 dBm to -9.6 dBm. The cords and optics are the same ones that worked before. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Fit an attenuator to each strand of that link
Clean the connector end faces on that link
Reseat the optics at both ends of that link
Swap the two strands at one end of that link
explanation: Each time a fiber connector is unplugged and handled, dust or skin oil can reach its end face, and contamination over the core blocks and scatters light, raising loss and causing errors. A 6.4 dB fall in receive power that began just after the connectors were handled points to their end faces, so inspecting them with a fiber scope and cleaning them is the right first step. Swapped strands would leave the receivers with no light at all, an attenuator is for a receiver that gets too much light, and the optics were not touched, so reseating them addresses nothing that changed.

question: One OSI layer opens, maintains and closes the dialog between two applications, and it can set checkpoints so that an interrupted exchange resumes where it stopped. Which layer is being described?
explanation: The Session layer (Layer 5) opens, maintains and closes the dialog between two applications, and it can set checkpoints from which an interrupted exchange resumes. Layer 4 (Transport) opens connections between hosts and resends lost data, but it does not manage the dialog of the applications. Layer 6 (Presentation) formats the data that is exchanged, and Layer 7 (Application) provides the network services that programs call on.

question: A company is choosing between PEAP and EAP-TLS for 802.1X on its wireless network. Which task does choosing PEAP allow the company to skip?
options: Registering each access point as a RADIUS client
Issuing each client device its own certificate
Creating a user account for each employee
Installing a certificate on the authentication server
explanation: PEAP authenticates the server with a certificate and then checks the user's password inside the resulting TLS tunnel, so clients need no certificates of their own, which EAP-TLS requires. The authentication server still needs its certificate, each access point must still be registered with the RADIUS server as a client, and each user still needs an account whose password is verified.

question: A contractor reaches the company's internal web applications from a personal laptop by signing in to an HTTPS portal in a web browser. Nothing else is installed on the laptop. Which type of VPN access is this?
explanation: A clientless VPN gives encrypted access to internal web applications through an HTTPS portal in an ordinary browser, so nothing has to be installed on the device. A remote-access IPSec VPN and a per-app VPN both need a VPN client or profile on the device, and a site-to-site VPN joins two networks through their gateways rather than serving one remote user.

question: Thousands of a bank's customers receive the same email, which claims that their account is locked and links to a fake sign-in page. Which attack is this?
explanation: Phishing sends the same deceptive message to large numbers of people, in the hope that some will follow the link and enter their credentials. Whaling aims a crafted message at one senior executive, vishing uses voice calls, and a watering hole attack infects a website that the intended victims already visit.

question: An engineer must capture every frame on a busy 10 Gbps fiber link between a firewall and a core switch for a week, including frames with errors. The capture must not depend on the switch's configuration or resources, and the link must keep working if the capture device fails. What should be installed?
options: A passive optical tap placed between the two devices
A fiber loopback plug fitted to a spare switch port
A protocol analyzer cabled to a free access port
A SPAN session that mirrors the firewall's switch port
explanation: A passive optical tap splits off a copy of the light in each direction, so it delivers every frame, damaged ones included, without any switch configuration or power, and the link keeps running even if the capture device fails. A SPAN session depends on the switch's configuration and resources, does not copy frames the switch discards as damaged, and can drop frames when a busy link exceeds the mirror port's capacity. An analyzer on an ordinary access port sees only its own traffic and what the switch floods to it, and a loopback plug tests a port rather than capturing traffic.

question: A growing firm replaces its peer-to-peer network with a client-server design. Which benefit should the firm expect from the change?
options: Less spending on hardware and licenses
Less effort to maintain user accounts
Less need for specialist IT staff
Less risk from a single point of failure
explanation: A client-server network keeps every user account in one directory on a server, so an account is created or changed once instead of on each PC. The other three are benefits of the peer-to-peer network that the firm is leaving: it needs no dedicated server hardware or server licenses, it can be run without specialist staff, and it has no single machine whose failure stops everyone from working.

question: A switch tags some of its syslog messages with severity 5. What does this severity indicate?
options: A routine event that needs no attention
A normal condition that is still significant
A problem that becomes an error if ignored
An internal event that helps developers
explanation: Notice, syslog severity 5, marks a condition that is normal but significant, such as a configuration change, so it deserves a look without being a fault. Warning (severity 4) flags a problem that will become an error if no action is taken, and Informational (severity 6) is for routine events that need no attention. Debug (severity 7) carries internal detail that helps developers and troubleshooters.

question: A data center team wants servers in any two racks to be the same number of switch hops apart. It also wants to add racks later by cabling each new top-of-rack switch to all four switches in the layer above. Which design meets both goals?
explanation: In a spine-and-leaf fabric every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, so servers in any two racks are the same number of hops apart and capacity grows by adding one leaf at a time. A three-tier hierarchy connects a new access switch only to its own distribution pair, so hop counts differ between parts of the network. A hub-and-spoke network has a single central node, and a full mesh links every switch directly to every other with no layers at all.

question: An audit of a newly installed switch finds its HTTP management page and a device discovery protocol running, although neither is used. Which hardening step addresses this finding?
explanation: Disabling services that are not needed, such as an unused web management page or discovery protocol, removes ways into the device and is a core step of device hardening.
